newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHIPPING SELLS FIVE DRY-CARGO VESELS FOR $9.5MLN.
newsitem.headline: SHIPPING SELLS FIVE DRY-CARGO VESELS FOR $9.5MLN.

text.p: The Latvian Shipping Company (LSC) said on Tuesday that it had sold five of its seven dry-cargo vessels for $9.5 million.
The shipping firm said in a statement the move was in line with its five-year development strategy aimed at scrapping unviable operations. It did not say who bought the ships.
The ships will remain under LSC's technical management for the next six months and full payment is due in August 1998, the comapny said.
LSC, the world's 19th largest shipping firm, said the age of the vessels ranged between 20 to 23 years.
"Continued use of these ships by the LSC could result in further losses," the statement said.
The LSC fleet includes 39 tankers, 24 refrigerated vessels and two gas vessels.
The company said it has entered a dry-cargo vessel pool arrangement with Maras Linija, with two vessels plying a Riga-Rotterdam-Felixstow-Hull route.
Each shipper provides one vessel under the arrangement and the profits are divided evenly.
"The first two voyages (this summer) have already earned LSC $36,000," the company said.
The LSC earlier reported a $35.49 million 1996 audited loss on turnover of $264.46 million. That was a 30 percent decrease in losses compared to 1995.
